t.1.161.1: Then, when she had vanished from sight, the king, the feller of hosts of enemies, bewildered by desire, fell to the surface of the earth.
t.1.161.3: Then the lovely maiden, in a sweet voice, addressed the king, that founder of the Kuru lineage, whose mind was stricken by desire.
t.1.161.2: When he had fallen to the ground, that sweetly smiling woman with full and broad hips once again showed herself to the king.
t.1.161.5: Thus addressed then in a sweet voice, the king saw that very woman of ample hips standing before him.
t.1.161.4: Rise, rise, blessings upon you! O tamer of foes, tiger among kings, renowned on earth as you are, you should not fall into delusion.
t.1.161.6: Then the king, his heart engulfed by the fire of love, addressed that dark-eyed maiden in a voice whose words faltered.
t.1.161.7: O dark-eyed one, O lady of intoxicating beauty, rightly accept me, tormented by desire; love me, for I love you, since my life-breaths are leaving me.
t.1.161.8: For it is on your account, O wide-eyed lady radiant as the heart of a lotus, that this Kāma keeps piercing me with his sharpened arrows and does not cease.
t.1.161.10: For my life-breaths depend on you, O you whose speech is like the song of the Kiṃnaras, O lovely one whose every limb is faultless, O you whose face is like the lotus and the moon.
t.1.161.9: O gracious lady, I am thus seized by the great serpent of desire, with no one to hear my cry. You, O lady of full and wide hips, O fair-faced one, must come and claim me.
t.1.161.11: For without you, timid one, I shall not be able to live by myself; therefore, wide-eyed lady, have compassion on me, fair woman.
t.1.161.12: O dark-eyed one, you should not forsake me, who am devoted to you; for you, O beautiful lady, ought to save me through the bond of love.
t.1.161.13: Come to me, timid one, by the Gāndharva form of marriage, O beautiful lady; for among marriages, O you with thighs like plantain stems, the Gāndharva is said to be the best.
t.1.161.14: I am not mistress of myself, O king, for I am a maiden whose father is living. If you have love for me, ask my father for my hand.
t.1.161.15: For just as your life-breaths have been captivated by me, O lord of men, so by the mere sight of you, you have carried off my life-breaths all the more.
t.1.161.16: I am not the mistress of my own body; therefore, O best of kings, I do not come near you, for women are not independent.
t.1.161.17: For what maiden in all the worlds would not desire as her lord and husband a king of renowned lineage, one who is tender toward those devoted to him?
t.1.161.18: Therefore, now that matters have come to this pass, ask my father Āditya for my hand, approaching him with humble prostration, with austerity and with self-restraint.
t.1.161.20: For I am named Tapatī, the younger sister of Sāvitrī, daughter of this Savitṛ, the lamp of the world, O bull among kṣatriyas.
t.1.161.19: If he wishes to give me to you, O crusher of foes, then, O king, I shall be ever obedient to your will.
